source.title: ELLE: Efficient Lifelong Pre-training for Emerging Data
source.authors: Yujia Qin; Jia-Jie Zhang; Yan-Kai Lin; Zhi-Yuan Liu; Peng Li; Maosong Sun; Jie Zhou

record.tranche_reason: Compares pretraining perplexity across width-only, depth-only, and combined expansion strategies with approximately matched parameter increases; this is a conceptual test of whether architecture details have little effect on loss.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work to motivate expansion, but does not fit power laws, test extrapolation, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The architecture-strategy comparison in Section 5 and Table 3 is relevant to V4. Other perplexity comparisons concern ELLE and lifelong-learning baselines; downstream scores and attention-pattern analyses do not test the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: ELLE cites Kaplan et al. for larger models being more sample-efficient and uses that as motivation for growing models during lifelong pre-training. Its results report its own method's performance. The Section 5 width/depth comparison is not a V4 test. Models are grown from a 30M ancestor by function-preserving expansion, trained under matched wall time rather than matched tokens, with replay across sequential domains. Parameter counts are only approximately matched (125M–129M at M5). The depth-only arm reaches 60 layers at d768, an extreme shape. AP differences therefore mix architecture with growth and inheritance efficiency and with unequal training steps. This measures progressive-growth efficiency, a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is that ELLE (function-preserved width/depth expansion with recovering warmup, plus pre-trained domain prompts) beats lifelong-learning baselines in pre-training efficiency and downstream performance at equal wall time. In the ablation, combined width+depth expansion is more efficient than either alone, with better downstream scores except on NS, and depth-only expansion is unstable. No scaling-law fits are drawn.
record.recipe_differences: The study concerns lifelong pre-training on sequential domain data, with function-preserving model expansion and memory replay; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law measurements or fit loss curves.
record.method_sensitivity: Expansion strategy changes pretraining AP; the authors report that depth-only expansion makes training unstable and that combined width-and-depth expansion is more efficient.

fits_no_version.finding: In progressive expansion of BERT from 30M to ~125M under matched wall time, combined width+depth growth gives lower AP than width-only or depth-only on Rev, Bio and CS (e.g. CS 4.13 vs 4.48/4.79). On NS it is nearly equal to depth-only (5.78 vs 5.81). Depth-only growth is reported as unstable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: When growing a pretrained model by function-preserving expansion, compound width+depth growth is more compute-efficient than single-dimension growth.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6 (Appendix A), fixed 7200 s per domain: expanding 2 layers/heads per stage gives the best AP (News 8.28, Review 7.25). Expanding 0, 4 or 6 does worse, so an intermediate expansion size is optimal under fixed compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under a fixed compute budget with weight inheritance, there is an intermediate optimal expansion size per growth stage.

record.problems: The architecture comparison covers a limited set of expansion strategies and only approximately matches parameter increases; the paper does not report uncertainty for the pretraining AP values.
record.rows_left_out: Perplexity results for lifelong-learning baselines, downstream F1 results, and attention-pattern or prompt analyses were omitted because they do not measure a claim version here. No scaling-law fit or extrapolation result is reported.

untested.parts: No compute-optimal N/D allocation. Table 6 (expansion size under fixed wall time) is confounded by weight inheritance.
No comparison of shapes trained from scratch at fixed parameter count and data.
No power-law fits in other modalities or regimes.
No downstream-vs-scale or downstream-vs-loss relation is fitted.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/V4 limits_scope is withdrawn. Shapes are compared only as growth paths from an inherited small model, with wall time rather than tokens matched, so the comparison cannot isolate shape effects on loss at fixed N. No uncertainty is reported for AP.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss relationships with parameter count, tokens, or compute over several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of much larger-run losses from power laws fitted on small runs.
The loss-minimizing allocation between parameters and tokens as compute changes.
The paper compares a limited set of expansion strategies at approximately matched parameter increases, not a broad sweep of architecture details at exactly fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and training regimes such as image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.
A predictable relationship between pretraining loss or scale and downstream-task performance.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Compared width-only, depth-only, and combined expansion strategies during BERT lifelong pre-training
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that combined expansion is more efficient than width-only or depth-only expansion; the AP values also differ across strategies (r1–r12). Parameter increases were only approximately matched, so this does not establish the effect at exactly fixed parameter count.
